text:
- chief complaint: the patient reports right wrist pain and swelling after a fall on stairs yesterday morning, with pain rated 9/10.
- history of present illness: the patient slipped while carrying laundry and fell onto outstretched arms, followed by severe right wrist pain and swelling. Ice, an ACE wrap, and ibuprofen give only partial relief. The patient has no prior injury to this arm and reports possible tingling in the fingers, which may be related to swelling.
- physical examination: right wrist shows marked swelling, ecchymosis, diffuse tenderness, pain with flexion, extension, radial and ulnar deviation, limited grip strength, and bony crepitus. Metacarpals are intact. Heart, lungs, neck, lower extremities, and upper extremity range of motion are unremarkable apart from the right wrist. Blood pressure is 140/70, heart rate about 80, respiratory rate 20, and afebrile. X-ray confirms an extra-articular Colles' fracture, possibly with dorsal angulation and ulnar styloid involvement.
- symptoms experienced by the patient: right wrist pain (9/10), swelling, bruising, reduced range of motion and grip, possible tingling in the fingers.
- new medications prescribed or changed: tramadol (Ultram) 50 mg every 6 hours for pain.
- follow-up instructions: surgical repair with screws is recommended as soon as possible, with an expected overnight stay. The patient should wear a brace for about six weeks and attend physical therapy about three times a week, starting after surgery. The patient should return in one month for a checkup to decide whether travel is advisable.
